### ① Derived judgments

Readings: card #12145 (body, triage 6109811077, claim 6110243674, dev report 6111181431); PR #12149 (body, the 45-file list, the net diff against `main` 158c75d); the 42 check-runs on the head; files at the head through the contents API. The "no call site" claims were read with `git grep` against the head commit's tree in the sibling repo's object store (a read of objects, no checkout, no run). Nothing built, run or re-run.

Every public-surface and accept-set change the diff implies, judged:

1. `@object-ui/i18n`: the `as const` `en` pack gains eight keys (`help.loadingDocumentation`, `common.breadcrumb`, `table.rowActions`, `fields.image.cropPreview`, `fields.percent.slider`, `designer.canvasMinimap`, `designer.versionHistory`, `grid.bulkActions`). `locales/en.ts` ends with `export type TranslationKeys = typeof en` and `index.ts:41` re-exports it, so the published type widens. All ten packs carry the eight with translated values, not English copies. RIGHT, a widening.
2. `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot`: `PromptInputAttachmentProps` gains an optional `removeLabel` whose default is the upstream English name; the element is public through `export * as AIElements from './elements'` and the elements barrel. RIGHT, a widening. `ChatbotEnhanced`'s `L.submit` / `L.stopResponse` fallbacks now read `console.ai.submit` / `console.ai.stopResponse` through the component's existing `tt = useSafeTranslate()`; a host `labels` value still wins (pinned). The `en` values are `Submit` and `Stop response`, the former literals, so the English name is unchanged. RIGHT. `L.removeAttachment` reads `detail.removeAttachment` only; there is no `labels.removeAttachment` arm, so a host cannot override that one name the way it can the others. An acceptable asymmetry, recorded as an acceptance note, not a breach.
3. `@object-ui/components`: `Spinner` names its status region `common.loading` through a `createSafeTranslation` hook whose test key is in its one-row defaults map; `aria-label` sits before `{...props}`, so a caller's name still wins. The `en` value is `Loading…` where the literal was `Loading`: the package's one English-name change, and the changeset names it. The `pagination` renderer passes `aria-label` to `PaginationPrevious` / `PaginationNext`; the No-Touch primitive (read at the head) puts its English default before `{...props}`, so the renderer's name wins and `ui/pagination.tsx` is untouched, as triage required. The `en` names become `Previous page` / `Next page`, the data-table pager's keys, and the changeset names that too. `DataTableRowActionsMenu` takes `t` as a prop and reads `table.rowActions`; `TABLE_DEFAULT_TRANSLATIONS` gains the row. RIGHT.
4. `@object-ui/fields`: the crop canvas, the percent slider and the record-picker grid read `useFieldTranslation` (`t` is already bound at `RecordPickerDialog.tsx:560`); `FIELD_DEFAULTS` gains three rows, one of them the borrowed `console.commandPalette.records` (`en` = `Records`). One key per name, as triage ruled. RIGHT.
5. `@object-ui/app-shell`: the `RecordFormPage` breadcrumb nav reads `common.breadcrumb` through its existing `t`. RIGHT.
6. `@object-ui/plugin-designer`: `HistoryPanel`, `Minimap`, `VersionHistory` and `DashboardDesignPage` read `useDesignerTranslation`; the defaults map gains five rows, `detail.goBack` borrowed (`en` = `Go back`). RIGHT.
7. `@object-ui/plugin-detail`: the `record-alert` dismiss button reads `home.recoveryReminder.dismiss` (`en` = `Dismiss`, `zh` = `关闭`) with an inline default; `record-path.tsx` changes a comment only, because the card's site there was a comment quoting an earlier repair and no attribute existed. RIGHT.
8. `@object-ui/plugin-grid`: the `BulkActionBar` region reads `grid.bulkActions` through its existing `t`. RIGHT.
9. `@object-ui/plugin-list`: the `TabBarSelect` trigger reads `topbar.switchView` (`en` = `Switch view`) through the already-imported `useObjectTranslation`; two `.find` lambdas are renamed so they stop shadowing `t`. RIGHT.
10. `@object-ui/console`: five docs pages read `help.loadingDocumentation` through `useObjectTranslation` (a declared dependency) with an inline default. RIGHT.
11. Exemptions, accept set unchanged, each verified against the head tree: `DebugPanel` (two names) is referenced only by its barrel export and a doc comment, no objectui surface mounts it; `ui/sidebar.tsx` `SidebarRail` is No-Touch and its only writer is `packages/cli/src/utils/app-generator.ts`, a generated-app template, with `aria-label` and `title` spread last so a host can name it; `elements/message.tsx` (four names) is vendored, has no call site outside the file, and spreads `props` after the defaults; `elements/prompt-input.tsx`'s `Submit` default is vendored and its sole call site, `ChatbotEnhanced`, overrides it. RIGHT, and the PR states each reason as the card's Done-when asks.
12. The vendored `prompt-input.tsx` edit: an additive optional prop with the upstream default preserved, on the `statusLabels` precedent (objectui#7254), present at `elements/tool.tsx:41-60`. The file header forbids editing business logic and asks for a wrapper; a wrapper cannot reach a button inside the chip, and a name prop is not business logic. The No-Touch register (`.claude/skills/objectui-contributor/rules/no-touch-zones.md`) covers `packages/components/src/ui/**` only. RIGHT. Re-sync hazard: a registry re-sync would restore the literal, and the census then reds on `prompt-input.tsx · Remove attachment`, so the hazard is guarded.
13. The census, `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/ariaLabelLiteralCensus-12145.test.ts`: a suite test, not a gate (triage's ruling); it walks every `packages/*` and `apps/*` `src/` tree minus tooling, judges four literal shapes with `\p{L}`, carries width guards, a lit control (a file directly under `src/`), and a matcher fixture; exemptions carry reasons; a frozen 87-name BACKLOG across 23 files is counted exactly, so a new literal and a removed declared one both red. Same shape and the same untyped `maskComments` import as the `machineLocaleCensus-9909` precedent. RIGHT.
14. The card's Done-when, re-measured on the head tree: the card's own re-check command returns exactly the ten exempt literals above and nothing else (31 at base). Per-package `zh` role-and-name pins exist for all nine packages touched (console by accessible name, see ③), and each `zh` case first asserts the two packs differ. RIGHT.

Finding confirmed: the card's pathspec, without `:(glob)`, reads no file directly under a `src/` root. `aria-label="Undo"` in `plugin-designer/src/DataModelDesigner.tsx` is unseen without it and seen with it; the same regex with `:(glob)` finds 114 sites at base and 93 at the head.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/12145-aria-label-i18n.md`: `@object-ui/i18n` minor, `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot` minor, the other eight touched packages patch. That is what the diff publishes: the only two type-surface widenings are `TranslationKeys` and `PromptInputAttachmentProps`; everything else is a behaviour fix in a released package (patch, never none). All ten are in the `fixed` group and `@object-ui/console` is versioned (`privatePackages.version: true`). The body names the eight keys, the new prop, and exactly the two `en` names that change, each checked against the `en` pack at the head. Not breaking, so no migration or ADR-0087 marker is owed. Gates: Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Declaration, Changeset Claim Re-read, Changeset Fixed Group Check, Changeset Overwrite Report, all success.

Clause-②: yes

The PR body's `Clause-②: yes` matches: a widening, `yes` takes at least minor, and both widened packages are minor. Triage's `no` was corrected in the claim on the `TranslationKeys` reasoning, which the head's declarations confirm.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `open_questions`: none. Deviations, each answered or escalated:

1. 87 literal sites frozen as census BACKLOG, not translated. ANSWERED for this PR: the claim's file surface is the card's 31 sites and the dev stopped at it, as the dispatch ordered; the card's Done-when is met as written. ESCALATED to the seat: the PR says `Fixes #12145`, so the queue would close "the family's closing card" with 87 names still literal (23 files, 11 packages; `auth`, `layout` and `plugin-map` carry no `@object-ui/i18n` dependency). Before arming, either file the follow-up card(s) from the dev's out-of-scope finding (a per-package slice is proposed) or turn `Fixes` into a non-closing reference so #12145 stays open. The seat's call, not a defect in the diff.
2. Edits beyond the 31 lines. ANSWERED: the pagination renderer, the defaults maps and `ChatbotEnhanced` are the claim's "wrapper or call site" and "translation-hook wiring"; the vendored prop is judged in ① 12; the two edited tests read the pack's name (the `zh-CN` case resolves through the registry's `zh-CN` to `zh` fallback) and add one case.
3. The console pin queries by accessible name, not role. ANSWERED: the spinner is an svg with no implicit role; `getByLabelText` reads the same accessible name a reader announces, and `apps/console` is an app, not one of the card's nine packages.
4. `TabBarSelect` lambda rename. ANSWERED: cosmetic, required by the new `t`.
5. The first commit subject says 26 names, the true count is 23. ANSWERED: history is not rewritten; the squash takes the PR title, which is right.
6. Queue timeouts. A process note, nothing to judge.

Also escalated to the seat, from the dev's acceptance notes (carrier none): 30 interpolating-template names need a ruling on how an interpolated name is keyed; `ChatbotEnhanced`'s `uploadFiles` fallback is still the English literal; visible English `Previous` / `Next` spans in the No-Touch pagination primitive and `SidebarTrigger`'s sr-only span. None is in the card's accept set.

Check-runs on the head, the reading as taken (42 runs): 35 success, among them Lint, Type Check, Build & E2E, Build Docs, Test (dist pins), Test shards 1/8, 3/8, 6/8 and 8/8, Governed Surface Queue Guard and the five changeset gates; 3 skipped (two matrix placeholders and dependabot); 4 in_progress: Test shards 2/8, 4/8, 5/8 and 7/8. Not a governed diff. The verdict below is the contract's; the landing still waits on the four shards' conclusions and on item 1 above.
